race: Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Welcome to Race Weekend, and Las Vegas just got spicy because the fastest man in qualifying is not starting up front.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Antonelli set the pace, but a grid penalty means Max Verstappen takes pole position on Sunday night in the city of lights.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: That is the story. Pole, Vegas form, recent wins, championship momentum, and a track where he has averaged second point three over three races.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: He has two podiums and a best of pole, so you cannot ignore that man when the city is lit up and the track is tricky.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: But George Russell is second on the grid, and he is the fastest second, which changes the whole shape of this race.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Fastest second, strong season, good Vegas history, average third point seven, best pole, two podiums over three races, and a car that looks sharp.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: So how do you beat Russell when the Mercedes rhythm is this strong and the car feels so confident in the night?

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: You trust the pace, the tyres, and the fact he can match Verstappen into the first corner and stay glued to the back bumper.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: And third is Kimi Antonelli, who was actually fastest in qualifying before the penalty changed the whole grid and the narrative.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: He starts sixth, but he has season form, car pace, and the kind of speed that can recover through a street circuit with traffic.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: He has one race history there, average third, best third, one podium, so he knows the groove and he knows how to push.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Can he charge through the chaos, avoid the mistakes, and still hit the podium on a track that rewards clean laps?

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I am not buying a clean top three if traffic blocks him, but the car is absolutely there and the confidence is huge.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Quick news before we go deeper: drivers are limited to twenty seven laps on a set of tyres at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: And if you want to follow Las Vegas on the BBC, the guide is out, so you can catch every lap of this night race.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: There is also a look inside an F1 helmet factory, and F1 bosses agreed a V8 engines deal from twenty thirty.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: That is a long one, but the big race story is still Russell fastest in practice after rain, which proves the pace is real.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Rain, practice speed, then Antonelli fastest in qualifying. Mercedes has been alive all weekend, and that is huge.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Deep cut for you: Charles Leclerc starts tenth, but Ferrari pace and Vegas history make him a real top five threat.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: That is the gamble. Ferrari can surge in the night, and Hamilton is right behind on eleventh, so both red cars can jump.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Lewis is there with championship form and the Ferrari car, so he can use experience to climb and maybe take a podium.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: And Isack Hadjar in fourth gives Red Bull another points chance, with Liam Lawson in seventh and Arvid Lindblad in fifth.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Wait, that is a lot of Red Bull and Racing Bulls pressure on the front group, and it could make the race harder to read.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Then Pierre Gasly in eighth is the low confidence top ten pick, with Alpine points form and second place speed.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: So my top ten is Max Verstappen, George Russell, Kimi Antonelli, Lando Norris, Charles Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Arvid Lindblad, Pierre Gasly.

segments.speaker: jake
segments.text: Say that again, because that is a lot of names and a lot of speed packed into one Las Vegas night race.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I hear you, but the grid says Max starts first, George starts second, and Kimi can still attack from sixth.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: That is the race we want, and Las Vegas is ready to deliver another night of chaos, speed, and glory. See you on Sunday night.
